12: Let us understand the Karnataka State Government's Agricultural Policy Landscape. The Karnataka state government directly shapes the agricultural environment in which an Agricultural Officer operates. Unlike central schemes, which are uniform across India, state schemes are tailored to Karnataka's specific soil types, crop patterns, and farmer demographics, and the Agricultural Officer is the primary field level implementation officer for these state schemes. The Siddaramaiah led Karnataka government, elected in 2023, made agriculture one of its focus areas, announcing the Five Guarantees, called Pancha Shakthi, of which Raitha Siri specifically targets farmers. Now, here is the Karnataka Agriculture Budget for 2025 to 26, key heads. The total agriculture department budget is over Rupees 4,500 crore, for extension, inputs, and infrastructure. The Krishi Bhagya scheme gets Rupees 800 crore, for farm ponds, watershed development, and drip irrigation. Raitha Siri, which is a PM Kisan top up, gets Rupees 500 crore, as a premium subsidy for small farmers. The PM Kisan state supplement gets Rupees 200 crore, as additional support to beneficiaries. And Bhoo Chethana, for soil and water, gets Rupees 300 crore, for soil testing and water conservation. There is also a field scenario box here, contrasting Raitha Siri with Telangana's Rythu Bandhu. A farmer asks why his cousin in Telangana gets Rupees 10,000 per acre, while he gets only Rupees 6,000 for his whole farm. The AO explains that Rythu Bandhu is calculated per acre in Telangana, while PM Kisan, which the farmer receives, is Rupees 6,000 per year per farmer family, regardless of land size, and Karnataka's Raitha Siri is a top up on PM Kisan for small and marginal farmers.
13: There is an important watch out box here. Do not confuse Karnataka's Raitha Siri with Telangana's Rythu Bandhu. They are different schemes, with different amounts and different eligibility criteria, and this is one of the most common traps in Karnataka PSC exams. There is also a quick checkpoint with two questions to test yourself. First, Karnataka's Raitha Siri scheme functions as what, on top of PM Kisan. Now we move to Section 1.2, Central Government Schemes Affecting Farmers, starting with the five schemes every AO must know cold. These five central schemes represent the backbone of agricultural welfare in India. They appear consistently in the examination and are equally relevant during field posting. The real measure of preparation is not just whether a candidate recognises these scheme names, but whether the concepts are understood well enough to explain them clearly to a farmer encountering them for the first time. Scheme 1 is PM Kisan, direct cash with no conditions. Launched in December 2018, the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi is arguably the simplest agricultural welfare scheme India has ever run. Every landholder farmer family gets Rupees 6,000 directly into their bank account every year, in three instalments of Rupees 2,000 each, with no conditions on how they spend it. Before PM Kisan, income support always came with strings attached, but PM Kisan removed all of that, transferring money directly with no middlemen and no conditions.
14: Now let us look at the complete PM Kisan scheme profile. The full name is Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi. It was launched in December 2018. The annual amount is Rupees 6,000 per farmer family per year, given in 3 instalments of Rupees 2,000 each. The instalment schedule follows three periods, April to July, August to November, and December to March. The transfer mode is Direct Benefit Transfer, DBT, directly to the bank. Eligibility covers all landholder farmer families. Exclusions include income tax payers, government employees, and large farmers, as defined by the state. The scheme is run by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. Karnataka coverage is around 50 lakh farmers, and the Karnataka supplement, Raitha Siri, provides a top up for small and marginal farmers. There is an important trick to remember here. Exam questions often ask about the instalment amount, Rupees 2,000, rather than the annual amount, Rupees 6,000, so know both. Also remember, PM Kisan was Rupees 6,000 from the very first instalment, it was never increased, so any option saying it was, quote, recently increased to Rupees 6,000, unquote, is wrong. A did you know box adds that PM Kisan has transferred over Rupees 3.04 lakh crore to more than 11 crore farmer families since its launch, making it one of the largest direct benefit transfer programmes in the world, with Karnataka alone having around 50 lakh beneficiary farmers.
